## What is still open
- **PR #247 is waiting on you**: Maya approves once CI is green and asked on the PR how many Orbitly events were dropped since #240 — you have the number (1,179,950 legitimate, ≈8.1% of their iOS volume) for Thursday's (19/11) Orbitly call [1][2].
- Once #247 is deployed, replay from landing for Orbitly (`prj_0rb1`) from 13/11 09:40 UTC (~1.18M events, ~40 min) and Zest (`prj_z3st`, 3,812), then confirm `ingest_dedupe_dropped_total` for `prj_0rb1` stays near zero — post-deploy only [1].
- Alert on the ingest dead-letter queue above 1,000 messages is due before Friday's (20/11) incident review [7].
- The note to the iOS team — restore UUID event_ids in kestrel-ios 3.2.1 — is drafted but not sent [1].

## What changed
- #233 postmortem is final; Noa presents it at Friday's incident review [3].
- Rachel Kim is closing Zest's Zendesk ticket in #support-escalations after their confirmation [6].

## What you did
- Diagnosed Orbitly's ~8% iOS funnel drop: #240's dedupe keys on event_id alone and kestrel-ios 3.2.0 sends per-session counters instead of UUIDs, so distinct events from different devices collided — 1,184,302 drops for Orbitly (99% of all projects), 1,179,950 legitimate; Zest lost 3,812 [1].
- Changed the dedupe key to `project_id:device_id:event_id` with tests (412 pass, lint clean) and opened PR #247 with Maya as reviewer [1].
